subject: BrightWave Dedicated Onboarding: pool topology, failover & burst policy
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Beth Carter <beth@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 22:02:00 +0000
Subject: BrightWave Dedicated Onboarding: pool topology, failover & burst policy

Hi Beth —

Great to see BrightWave move forward. Attached is a short checklist and two topology options for Dedicated GPU pools: single-region with warm standby and active-active multi-region. High level asks from our side before the kickoff: 

- Confirm preferred region(s) for primary capacity (us-west-2 / us-east-1).
- Any hard data residency or egress restrictions?
- Expected peak concurrent tokens/min and 95th percentile latency target.
- Procurement timeline / PO cadence (we'll need that for capacity commit).

Proposal highlights in the attached SOW draft: 
- Autoscaling: target-based policy using sustained CPU/GPU utilization + pending queue length; typical warm-burst window = 5–10 minutes.
- Burst: short-term burst capacity available from a shared regional buffer; charged at burst-rate until steady-state is reached.
- Failover: cross-region passive failover (KV-cache rebuild on failover) — recommended for low RTO but slightly higher failover latency.

I've attached: brightwave-network-diagram.pdf and sow-draft-brightwave-v1.docx.

Propose a technical kickoff Wed 17 Jun 10:00–11:00 PT. Does that work for your engineering + procurement?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198


From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: BrightWave Dedicated Onboarding: pool topology, failover & burst policy

Kim — quick notes after skimming the SOW and diagram: 

- For BrightWave's stated throughput (you mentioned ~120k tokens/min peak in the call), recommend a 2-zone active-active design in us-west-2 to avoid cross-region egress costs and keep KV-cache locality. Multi-region only if they need explicit DR across regions.
- Autoscaling: we should set two thresholds: a conservative ramp-to-burst threshold (85% GPU util over 120s) and an aggressive emergency burst policy (95% util + queue depth) that uses the shared buffer. That keeps latency SLO intact while limiting cost.
- Quantization: suggest shipping 8-bit quantized variants for lower-memory models to reduce ECUs during steady-state. Marcus

Cc: Sean for ops impact, Monica for CS coordination.

Marcus
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference


From: Beth Carter <beth@brightwave.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: James Li <james.li@brightwave.ai>, procurement@brightwave.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: BrightWave Dedicated Onboarding: pool topology, failover & burst policy

Thanks, Kimberly — the Wed 17 Jun 10:00 PT kickoff works for engineering and procurement. A few items from our side: 

- Primary region: us-west-2. We'd prefer single-region with warm standby in us-east-1 unless you feel strongly about active-active. Our priority is data locality and predictable egress.
- Data residency: all inference payloads must remain in-region; no model logging to external buckets without explicit consent.
- Latency SLO: 95th < 220ms for chat endpoints.
- Peak: estimating 140k tokens/min during campaign bursts; steady-state ~20k tokens/min.
- Procurement: procurement will need SOW + pricing table and a standard PO template before the kickoff. They asked if the burst rate is capped and how billing will show burst consumption vs committed units.

We'll review the SOW draft and send procurement questions separately.

Best,
Beth Carter
VP Product Engineering | BrightWave AI
beth@brightwave.ai


From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Beth Carter <beth@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 17:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: BrightWave Dedicated Onboarding: pool topology, failover & burst policy

Beth — thanks for the clarity. Quick replies inline: 

- Region: us-west-2 primary + warm standby us-east-1 is a good fit given your residency ask. We'll keep logs and KV caches regional by default; audit logs can be retained per your retention policy — we'll coordinate KMS keys in the kickoff.
- Latency: we'll aim for 95th < 200ms in our test runs; production SLAs will depend on model selection and sequence lengths but we'll validate in soak tests.
- Peak handling & billing: burst is capped by the size of the shared regional buffer we allocate during onboarding. Billing will show committed capacity (monthly) + burst usage at a defined burst rate line item. I'll attach a pricing extract before kickoff.

Action items before Wed kickoff: 
- BrightWave: confirm PO timeline and send procurement contact details (name + phone).
- Redwood: circulate final SOW v1.1 with pricing extract, and pre-kickoff runbook (ops-runbook-stub.md).

I'll follow up with a calendar invite.

Kim

Subject: RE: BrightWave Dedicated Onboarding: pool topology, failover & burst policy

Hi Kimberly / Monica —

Procurement here. A few items we need before we can issue a PO: 
1) Final SOW with line-item pricing and clear burst pricing caps (we need the per-token or per-minute burst rate).
2) Standard MSSA / Data Processing Appendix or confirmation that Redwood will sign BrightWave's DPA.
3) Billing contacts and invoicing cadence (monthly in arrears is preferred).

Also: we need an initial estimated start-of-service date. Can Redwood commit to a turn-up in 6 weeks from PO? If not, provide a standard lead time and any prerequisites (network peering, KMS setup, IP allowlist).

Please send the items as attachments to this thread and cc finance@brightwave.ai.

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 16:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: BrightWave Dedicated Onboarding: pool topology, failover & burst policy

Looping ops & SRE in as requested. Quick implementation plan (high level):

1) Pre-provisioning (Week 0–1): network peering request from BrightWave (list of allowed IPs), KMS key exchange, sign DPA / MSSA.
2) Provisioning (Week 2–3): allocate GPU pool in us-west-2 (primary) + warm standby in us-east-1. Initial pool sized for 140k tokens/min with headroom for 10% growth.
3) Validation (Week 4): soak tests with sample loads, latencies measured against 95th < 220ms target; KV-cache priming and quantized-model smoke tests.
4) Cutover (Week 5–6): DNS / routing change and runbook-driven failover drills.

I've attached ops-runbook-stub.md to this thread for the kickoff; it contains checklist items we will expand. If procurement can sign within 5 business days and provide peering details within 10 business days, 6-week turn-up is achievable.

Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
